However, the new specs `spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb` and `spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb` only assert the classes inherit from `Admin::AdminController` and provide no coverage for the new behaviors/endpoints, so the advisory about vacuous controller specs and missing regression coverage is accurate and diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] SQL injection via unescaped interpolation in migration INSERT of raw `embeddable_hosts` setting value without sanitizing quotes, breaking the migration on values containing quotes.

adjudication.rationale: The migration `20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb` builds raw SQL with unescaped interpolation: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"` where `h` comes from the `embeddable_hosts` site setting value split by newlines. If any host line contains a single quote (or other SQL-breaking characters), the migration can fail; additionally, interpolating unsanitized data into SQL is a SQL injection risk (even if the source is a prior setting value).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Failed sub-type lookups in store.js.es6 plural hydration leak `false` entries into the hydrated array; `hydrated || []` doesn't rescue, and no test covers an id missing from side-loaded payload.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6`, the new plural hydration branch (`/(.+)\_id(s?)$/` with `if (m[2])`) builds `hydrated` via `obj[k].map(id => this._lookupSubType(...))` and then assigns `obj[self.pluralize(subType)] = hydrated || []`. Since `map` always returns an array (truthy) even if lookups fail, missing side-loaded records will produce `false`/undefined entries that are not filtered out, so `hydrated || []` does not prevent leaking invalid entries into the hydrated array. The updated JS tests only cover the fully-side-loaded case (`color_ids` with `colors` present) and do not cover a missing id scenario.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] EmbeddableHost validation regex permits paths/ports the exact-match lookup can never match, before_validation stripping is silently lossy, and case-differing duplicate hosts are accepted with no uniqueness validation or spec coverage.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/models/embeddable_host.rb`, the validation regex allows ports and paths (`(:[0-9]{1,5})?(\/.*)?`), but `before_validation` only strips protocol and path (it does not strip `:port`). Meanwhile `record_for_host` parses the referer via `URI(host).host`, which returns only the hostname without the port, and then does `where("lower(host) = ?", host)`. So a saved record like `example.com:3000` can be valid/persisted but will never match any referer lookup (which becomes `example.com`), breaking `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?` checks introduced in `embed_controller`/`topic_retriever`. The lack of uniqueness/case-normalization is also visible (no `uniqueness` validation and lookup is case-insensitive), but the port mismatch is a concrete behavior bug shown by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Migration inserts legacy host values verbatim without running before_validation normalization that strips http:// prefixes and paths, so upgraded sites with hosts carrying a scheme or path have all embeddable hosts silently stop working (embed comments return 403) since record_for_host compares a bare hostname

adjudication.rationale: The migration `20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb` copies legacy `site_settings.embeddable_hosts` values into the new `embeddable_hosts.host` column via raw SQL (`execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, ...) VALUES ('#{h}', ...)"`), which bypasses the model’s `before_validation` normalization in `EmbeddableHost` that strips `http(s)://` and paths. Since `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` parses the incoming URL and compares `where("lower(host) = ?", uri.host)`, any migrated rows stored with a scheme/path (e.g. `https://example.com/1234`) will not match `uri.host` (`example.com`), causing `host_allowed?` to return false and embedding requests to be rejected.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Migration crashes with NoMethodError on sites where embed_category was never set because the SELECT for the site_settings row returns no result; category_id == 0 fallback never executes since line 18 fails first
matched_golden_ids: The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same root cause: the migration assumes the SELECT returns at least one row and immediately dereferences execute(...)[0]['id'], which crashes (e.g., NoMethodError) when no embed_category site_setting exists, preventing the intended fallback/behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Host values from the legacy setting are interpolated directly into a SQL string literal; a value containing a single quote breaks or corrupts the INSERT and aborts the migration — use quote or AR records
[BUG] update and destroy in EmbeddableHostsController fetch by id without a nil check; a stale-id PUT/DELETE crashes with NoMethodError returning a 500 instead of a 404

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#update` and `#destroy`, the record is fetched via `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` with no handling for a missing record. If the id is stale/nonexistent, `host` will be `nil` and `save_host(host)` will call `host.host = ...` (NoMethodError) and `host.destroy` in `destroy` will also raise, causing a 500 instead of a 404/handled error.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Admin::EmbeddingController#update re-renders the serializer without reading any params — a no-op endpoint with no consumer in this diff; delete it or scope the change to actual embedding settings

The diff also shows a consumer (`admin/controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6` `saveChanges()` calls `this.get('embedding').update({});`), but it submits `{}` and nothing on the server can change anyway. This is a real scope/API design issue, not a functional defect proven by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Hot-path regression: ensure_embeddable previously used the cached SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts but now runs an uncached SQL query on every embed comments request, adding a per-request DB round-trip on high-traffic embed pages

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` from checking `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?(request.referer)` (string parsing of cached settings) to `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?(request.referer)` (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb). `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?` calls `record_for_host`, which executes `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first` (app/models/embeddable_host.rb), i.e., a DB query per request. The diff shows no caching layer around this lookup, so the advisory about adding a per-request DB round-trip is grounded. This is a performance concern rather than a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The embeddable_hosts migration backfill inserts raw setting lines without running the model's before_validation normalization (stripping scheme/path), so lookups comparing lower(host) = uri.host fail and hosts that could embed before the upgrade get rejected after deploys

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the backfill copies each legacy `embeddable_hosts` line verbatim into the new `embeddable_hosts.host` column via raw SQL (`INSERT ... VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`). This bypasses the EmbeddableHost model's `before_validation` normalization that strips `http(s)://` and paths. Later, authorization uses `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?(request.referer)` -> `record_for_host` -> `where("lower(host) = ?", uri.host)`, which compares against the normalized `uri.host` (e.g., `discourse.org`). If the migrated row is stored as `http://discourse.org` or `https://example.com/1234`, the lookup will fail and previously-allowed hosts can be rejected after upgrade.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] record_for_host compares lower(host) against uri.host while the write path preserves case and port (validation allows mixed case, before_validation strips only scheme and path), so just-saved hosts like Example.com or example.com:8080 are rejected at the embed boundary

[BUG] Admin::EmbeddableHostsController update/destroy call save_host/host.destroy on the result of where(id:).first with no nil check, raising NoMethodError (500) instead of 404 for stale or nonexistent ids

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#update` and `#destroy`, the code does `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then immediately calls `save_host(host)` / `host.destroy` without checking for `nil`. If the record doesn’t exist (stale/nonexistent id), `save_host` will call `host.host = ...` and raise `NoMethodError`, and `destroy` will raise on `host.destroy`, resulting in a 500 instead of a 404/not-found response.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The embeddable_hosts table has no unique index on host and no index on category_id, while every embed request does a non-sargable where("lower(host) = ?") full scan on the hot embed path, and duplicate hosts can be saved leaving indistinguishable rows that still grant access

adjudication.rationale: The migration `CreateEmbeddableHosts` creates `embeddable_hosts` without a unique constraint/index on `host` (and no index at all). The model lookup used on the embed hot path is `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` which queries `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first`, so duplicates are possible and deletion of one row would not necessarily revoke access if another duplicate remains (still makes `host_allowed?` true). This is a real behavioral/security defect enabled by the diff; the perf/indexing concern is also grounded (no supporting index for this query).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The host regex allows an optional port tail that before_validation keeps but uri.host lookup always strips, so a saved example.com:8080 host is permanently locked out of embedding despite a green success UI

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbeddableHost`, the validation regex allows an optional port (`...(:[0-9]{1,5})?`), and `before_validation` strips scheme and path but does not strip the port (only `sub!(/^https?:\/\//, '')` and `sub!(/\/.*$/, '')`). However, `record_for_host` parses the referer/url with `URI(host)` and then uses `uri.host`, which omits the port, and queries `where("lower(host) = ?", host)`. So a saved DB value like `example.com:8080` will never match a lookup for `http://example.com:8080/...` (lookup host becomes `example.com`), permanently rejecting embeds for that entry.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The embeddable-host save flow sets category via Discourse.Category.findById(categoryId) with no nil guard and categoryId defaults to null for new hosts, so the UI can show a category state diverging from the persisted record

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6`, `categoryId` is initialized to `null` and is only set in `edit()` (from `host.category.id`) or via the chooser. For a new host (`host.isNew`), `editing` is true immediately but `categoryId` can remain `null`. On `save()`, the client sends `props.category_id = this.get('categoryId')` (possibly null), while the server (`Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host`) coerces blank `category_id` to `SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id`. After the save resolves, the client unconditionally runs `host.set('category', Discourse.Category.findById(this.get('categoryId')))`, which will be `findById(null)` and can set `category` to `undefined`, diverging from the persisted category_id chosen by the server.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] expandable_first_post? drops the SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present? guard, leaving the 'no hosts → never expandable' invariant enforced only by incidental coupling with TopicEmbed.import, so a future writer of TopicEmbed rows could silently re-enable truncation-expansion

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes Topic#expandable_first_post? from `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present? && SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?` to `SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?` (app/models/topic.rb), and the `embeddable_hosts` site setting is removed in favor of the EmbeddableHost table. There is no replacement guard like `EmbeddableHost.exists?`, so expandability is now controlled only by `embed_truncate` and the presence of a TopicEmbed row. That does create tighter coupling to how TopicEmbed rows get created (TopicEmbed.import now consults EmbeddableHost.record_for_host), and it could allow expansion behavior even when no EmbeddableHost records exist (e.g., if hosts are deleted after embeds exist, or if TopicEmbed rows are created by some other path). This is a real, diff-grounded design/behavior concern, but it’s not a clearly provable defect from the diff alone because the intended invariant after migrating away from the setting isn’t specified.

VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"`. The value `h` comes from the existing `site_settings` value `embeddable_hosts` (user/admin-controlled text) and is not quoted/escaped. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] `update` action in embedding_controller renders the embedding but never saves, making the PUT endpoint a silent no-op that discards admin changes with a 200 response

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddingController#update`, the method simply re-renders the serialized `@embedding` (an `OpenStruct` built in `fetch_embedding`) and does not persist any parameters (`render_serialized(@embedding, ...)` with no mutation). However, the diff’s actual admin edits (adding/updating/deleting allowed hosts) are performed via the separate `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController` (`create/update/destroy` save to `EmbeddableHost`). The client template `admin/templates/embedding.hbs` also does not invoke `saveChanges`, so the PUT `/admin/customize/embedding` endpoint appears unused in the shown UI. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] embed_controller error message conflates 'embeddable hosts not set' with 'invalid referer host', reporting the latter even when zero hosts exist, misleading admins debugging fresh setups

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`, the prior explicit check for missing configuration (`raise ... 'embeddable hosts not set' if SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.blank?`) was removed and replaced with a single check: `raise ... 'invalid referer host' unless EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?(request.referer)` (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb). When there are zero `EmbeddableHost` records, `host_allowed?` will return false, causing the controller to always raise 'invalid referer host' even though the real problem is that no hosts are configured. This matches the finding: the error message is now misleading in fresh/empty setups.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Removal of `embeddable_hosts` and `embed_category` site settings is breaking and non-reversible: `db:rollback` drops the table without restoring settings, and legacy-invalid host rows become uneditable with no fix path short of deletion

adjudication.rationale: The migration `CreateEmbeddableHosts` uses `def change` with multiple raw `execute` statements (including inserting rows and `DELETE FROM site_settings ...`). In Rails, migrations containing non-reversible operations like `execute` inside `change` are typically treated as irreversible, so `db:rollback` will fail (or at minimum cannot restore the deleted `embeddable_hosts`/`embed_category` settings). This makes the removal of those settings effectively non-reversible from the DB. The additional claim about “legacy-invalid host rows become uneditable” is not clearly verifiable from the diff (server-side `before_validation` normalizes `host` on save), but the rollback/data-loss concern is grounded in the migration shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Host values are interpolated directly into raw SQL (`VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`) with no quoting/parameterization, so any host value containing a single quote breaks the INSERT mid-migration while the unconditional DELETE still destroys the source data

adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point to the same root problem: host values are inserted into raw SQL via string interpolation without parameter binding/quoting. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] `create_table :embeddable_hosts, force: true` is destructive on re-run: on a database where embeddable_hosts already has rows, the table is dropped and all host/category configuration is lost with no way to re-migrate since the source rows were already deleted

adjudication.rationale: The migration `CreateEmbeddableHosts` uses `create_table :embeddable_hosts, force: true`, which will drop and recreate the table if it already exists, causing loss of any existing `embeddable_hosts` rows. The same migration also deletes the original source settings (`execute "DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')"`), so if the migration were ever re-run against a DB where the table already exists, the dropped data cannot be rehydrated from `site_settings` because that source was removed on the first run.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The migration is irreversible: `def change` contains irreversible raw execute statements (the settings DELETE) with no up/down split, and the deleted site_settings rows were never backed up, so rolling back past this migration permanently loses old embeddable_hosts/embed_category values

adjudication.rationale: The new migration `20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb` uses `def change` but contains multiple raw `execute` statements that are not automatically reversible, including `execute "DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')"`. There is no explicit `up`/`down` (or `reversible` block) to recreate the deleted `site_settings` rows on rollback, so rolling back past this migration would both be irreversible in Rails and would permanently lose the prior `embeddable_hosts` / `embed_category` values.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The category_id == 0 fallback reads uncategorized_category_id via raw SQL which may be nil on fresh installs, yielding category_id of 0 that violates the null:false constraint or inserts an orphaned reference (no FK defined), causing TopicEmbed.import to create embedded topics in an invalid category or fail

adjudication.rationale: In the migration `20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`, the fallback logic assumes `site_settings` rows exist and are non-nil: it does `execute("SELECT value FROM site_settings WHERE name = 'uncategorized_category_id'")[0]['value'].to_i` and later inserts rows with that `category_id`. If the query returns no rows (or `value` is NULL), `[0]` will be nil (raising) or `to_i` will yield `0`, and the migration will either fail or create `embeddable_hosts.category_id = 0` despite `null: false` and with no guarantee such a category exists. That can then propagate via `TopicEmbed.import` using `eh.try(:category_id)` to create topics with an invalid category id.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host(url)` returns false/nil on mismatch and `category: eh.try(:category_id)` becomes nil, silently replacing the old SiteSetting.embed_category behavior with no-category, creating topics with an unintended default category with no warning or log

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the category assignment changed from a global `SiteSetting.embed_category` to per-host lookup: `eh = EmbeddableHost.record_for_host(url)` and `category: eh.try(:category_id)` (app/models/topic_embed.rb). If `record_for_host` returns `false`/`nil` (e.g., URL not parseable or no matching host record), `eh.try(:category_id)` becomes `nil`, and the code provides no fallback or explicit error/log. The diff does not prove this will actually create topics in an unintended default category in normal embed flows (since other code now checks `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?`), but it is a concrete, diff-grounded behavioral edge case worth flagging.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The embed_category lookup joins on s.value = c.name, but the stored setting string includes YAML quoting (e.g. "'General'"), so the join fails even for sites that set embed_category to an exact category name, silently degrading all per-embed category preferences to uncategorized

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Code reading the old settings is removed in the same commit as the migration creating the new table with no expand+contract window; rolling deploys where code and migration aren't atomic call EmbeddableHost against a non-existent table and 500 on every /embed/comments request

adjudication.rationale: The diff switches runtime checks from `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?` to `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?` in hot paths like `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` and `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?`, while the `embeddable_hosts` table is only introduced via the new migration `20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb` and the old settings-based logic/settings are removed in the same change. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The backfill runs inside the migration using raw SQL, bypassing the model's before_validation normalization and format validation, so migrated rows keep http:// and paths in host which fail EmbeddableHost's regex on edit and never match a referer via record_for_host's exact-match, silently rejecting hosts that worked pre-migration

adjudication.rationale: The migration `CreateEmbeddableHosts` backfills by directly executing `INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, ...) VALUES ('#{h}', ...)` using the raw `site_settings` line `h` (which, per prior behavior/tests, could include `http://` / `https://` and/or paths like `https://example.com/1234`). This bypasses `EmbeddableHost`'s `before_validation` normalization that strips schemes and paths. Later, authorization checks use `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host(request.referer)` which parses the referer URL and matches `where("lower(host) = ?", uri.host)`, so stored values like `http://discourse.org` or `example.com/1234` will not match `discourse.org` / `example.com`, causing embeds to be rejected post-migration even if they previously worked. Additionally, such rows would fail the model format validation if edited/saved through the model layer.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] update and destroy in app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:13 fetch EmbeddableHost by id with no nil check, causing NoMethodError on nil and a raw 500 instead of a 404 for nonexistent or already-deleted ids (hit by the UI delete() path on stale data)

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] save() in app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6:30-40 relies on categoryId only initialized in the edit() action, so a new (isNew) host saved without touching the category chooser is created with category_id: null (server substitutes uncategorized) and the client's post-save category object is wrong until reload, with no signal distinguishing 'never chose' from 'chose uncategorized'

adjudication.rationale: In app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6, categoryId is initialized to null and only set in the edit() action (this.set('categoryId', this.get('host.category.id'))). For a new host, `editing` is true via `Ember.computed.or('host.isNew', 'editToggled')`, so save() can be invoked without ever calling edit(). In save(), it unconditionally sends `props.category_id = this.get('categoryId')` (null) and the server substitutes uncategorized when blank (Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host sets uncategorized_category_id if blank). After save, the client sets `host.category` using `Discourse.Category.findById(this.get('categoryId'))`, which is still null, leaving the client-side category relationship wrong/empty until reload even though the server persisted uncategorized.
